newsitem.title: POLAND: ZLOTY SLIPS VS BASKET, C.BANK CAPS DRAINAGE RATES.
newsitem.headline: ZLOTY SLIPS VS BASKET, C.BANK CAPS DRAINAGE RATES.

text.p: The zloty eased slightly against the basket of currencies amid a light currency-buying trend on Wednesday, and dealers expected it stay at around the support level of minus one percent from the parity rate on Thursday.

"There was some pressure on the zloty to weaken today and the local unit should remain between 0.7 and 1.0 weaker than parity on Thursday...but it may test support next week," said Witold Wozniak, forex dealer at Deutsche Bank Polska SA.
Polish financial markets are closed for holiday on Friday.
The zloty closed 0.83/0.95 percent weaker than its trading band centre down from Tuesday's minus 0.78/0.90 percent.
It closed at 3.4860/00 to the dollar, against 3.4839/79 on Tuesday and at 1.8875/00 to the mark, against 1.8770/91.

Dealers said no larger foreign investment inflows followed Monday's central bank warning that it may further tighten its monetary policy in the near-term to cap credit growth, but that foreign currency speculators were active on Wednesday.
"Foreign players were active in both directions, they sold the dollar, but some were also leaving the market," said Mariusz Wituszynski, forex dealer at Kredyt Bank SA.
On Wednesday the central bank capped its main drainage rate at 23.55 percent after raising it to that level on Tuesday.
Dealers said that today's NBP actions signalled that the central bank would likely keep its drainage rates flat for the upcomming weeks before potentially raising them again.
"For now, the new market rates seem to satisfy the central bank, but it is possible that this might change in a week or two," said Adam Gadomski, dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.
On the money market one-day rates remained flat around 23.10 percent despite the central bank's 198 million zloty 14-day reverse repo and 658 million 91-day NBP-bill sale.
One-day rates should rise next week as firms pay monthly taxes around August 20. -- Tomasz Oljasz +48 22 653 9700
